title: From Shoot to Edit: An Ingest and Dailies Workflow for Remote Teams
summary: Plan a remote dailies workflow from verified camera-card offload to upload, review, and the editor's receiving checks, with clear ownership at each handoff.
body_markdown:
A remote editor can open a dailies link and still be missing production sound or camera originals, or find that the review files have the wrong look baked in. When you send the link, tell the editor which files are ready and which are still being prepared so they can plan the session.


Dailies are the viewing copies prepared from a shoot for the director, producers, and editors to review. Ingest means copying the recorded media into the production's storage, verifying the copies, and keeping the camera and sound records with the files. Agree on which viewing files and editing media your team needs in each delivery, then have the receiving editor confirm they arrived.


## Agree on the delivery before the first card arrives


Write a short workflow memo with the post supervisor, camera department, production sound team, and assistant editor. Specify the camera formats, timeline frame rate, sound arrangement, review target, proxy requirements, folder structure, and delivery deadlines. Include the people who can resolve an exception when a roll arrives late or a transfer fails.


Assign someone on your team to each stage, even when one person handles several jobs. For example, a two-camera production could divide the work as follows:


Stage Named owner Evidence passed to the next person


Camera and sound offload Maya, data wrangler Card inventory, copy destinations, and verification reports


Dailies preparation Luis, dailies operator Synced viewing files, editing proxies, color references, and exceptions


Cloud transfer Maya Completed batch inventory and any outstanding transfers


Media accepted for editing Noor, assistant editor Import, sync, proxy, and source-access checks


Card release and unresolved exceptions Rowan, post supervisor Recorded decision under the production's media policy


Set separate deadlines when reviewers and editors need different material, such as selected takes for the director that evening and the complete day's footage, wild sound, and camera reports for the editor the following morning. The memo should also say whether camera originals must reach the remote location before editing begins or can arrive after validated proxies.


A small viewing file reaches the editor first while the larger originals travel behind it.


## Offload the complete card and retain the verification record


Maya begins each batch by recording the shoot date, camera or recorder ID, card ID, and source volume name. Each card goes into a uniquely named container that preserves its internal folder structure, filenames, and sidecars. Dailies renders belong outside those original-media containers so later verification has a stable source package to compare.


Use a checksum-verifying offload tool. A checksum is a value calculated from a file's contents; comparing the source and destination values helps detect changes introduced during copying.[ARRI's data-transfer guidance](https://www.arri.com/en/learn-help/learn-help-camera-system/pre-postproduction/data-transfer) recommends creating these records when media first leaves the camera card and retaining them through archival.


Check the tool's verification mode as well as its completion message. For example,[OffShoot distinguishes transfer, source, and source-and-destination verification](https://docs.hedge.video/offshoot/features/verification) . Those modes perform different checks, so choose the mode required by the production's media policy rather than assuming every completed transfer includes a destination read-back.


In this example, the policy requires two independently verified storage destinations before Rowan can release a card. Maya records both destination results and keeps the source manifest, which lists the files and their checksums, with the handoff records. An error leaves that card on hold until the issue is resolved. The[checksum-offload guide](https://aspect.inc/blog/post-production/how-to-verify-media-offloads-with-checksum-tools) covers algorithm selection and verification tooling in greater detail.


One camera card branches to two copied drives, each shown under comparison. Record file counts and camera clip counts separately. One playable clip can involve several files, while camera cards can also contain sidecars and databases. An inventory showing 86 playable clips may still be missing sidecars or other files from the cards. Reconcile the file inventory, total bytes, and the expected playable clips, then investigate any discrepancy.


## Upload each batch with its file inventory


Use one batch identifier everywhere, such as` DAY03_20260928` . Keep the camera-card containers intact underneath it, and put derived media and reports in their own locations:


```text
DAY03_20260928/
Originals/
Camera_A/A021/
Camera_B/B014/
Sound/S003/
Dailies/
Editing_Proxies/
Reports/
Color_References/


```


The upload can come from a verified local copy, allowing production to retain its working and backup copies while the remote delivery runs. Aspect[preserves nested folders during upload](https://aspect.inc/docs/getting-started/uploading-and-organizing) , shows batch progress, and lets you pause and resume transfers.


Estimate how long the upload will take on the connection you'll use at the shoot. If the connection can't move the day's originals in time, prioritize the agreed viewing files, validated editing proxies, sound, and reports, and keep the originals transfer listed as outstanding. Before the editor starts with proxies, agree on how they connect to the originals and when those originals will arrive.


Maya reconciles the completed upload with the batch inventory before marking it transferred. Aspect's transfer status provides progress information; the verification reports in this workflow come from the separate offload and receiving tools. If the production requires a fully verified receiving copy, retrieve the complete originals and compare them with the source manifest. That check reads the whole delivery and needs its own time and bandwidth allowance.


## Prepare viewing dailies and editing proxies for their different uses


Luis prepares viewing files for the director and producer, plus proxies that work with the editing application. One set of files can serve both purposes if it has the right picture treatment, source mapping, and audio layout.


For review, check that the picture is correctly framed, the sound is synchronized, and the intended color treatment is applied. If the camera recorded separately from the sound recorder, retain the original sound files and record how they map to the camera clips. Check synchronization at multiple points in longer takes; matching at the slate alone may miss drift or an incorrect interpretation of the recording rate.


Confirm the camera input, look version, and output viewing target before rendering the batch. When the review needs to show the approved look and shot-level corrections, render dailies with that treatment and compare them with the approved reference stills. The[color-managed dailies guide](https://aspect.inc/blog/post-production/how-to-set-up-color-managed-dailies-that-match-the-on-set-look) covers the transform order and color handoff in detail.


Record each proxy's source camera filename and roll ID in the delivery manifest so the editor can identify its original. Check source timecode, frame rate, duration, image interpretation, and audio-channel layout against the editing application's requirements. Decide whether the editor will use separately synchronized sound or audio carried in the proxy, and test that arrangement before rendering a full day.


You can[copy uploaded videos as smaller MP4 proxies in Aspect](https://aspect.inc/docs/workflows/premiere-pro) and attach them to originals in Premiere. If the project calls for a particular codec or audio layout, create the proxies in Premiere with those settings. After attachment, toggle between a proxy and its original to check that the picture and sound match.


## Review a complete, identified set of dailies


Upload completion doesn't mean browser processing has finished. Aspect begins preparing playback, transcripts, and search information after upload, with results appearing as they become ready. Check the[processing indicators](https://aspect.inc/docs/asset-intelligence/ai-indexing) and open the intended review files before announcing that the viewing set is available.


Luis checks the technical delivery before Rowan sends it for creative review. Include clips from every camera and recording mode used on the shoot, check every reported exception, and complete any full-length review required by the production. Record which clips were checked so the recipient knows whether the whole batch was reviewed.


Give the review collection a batch name, an explanation of what it contains, and a feedback deadline. Configure[sharing permissions](https://aspect.inc/docs/share-and-present/sharing-and-permissions) for the audience, including commenting, downloads, and visible metadata. Use comments on the relevant frame for picture or sync issues, and identify who will investigate them.


Keep technical readiness separate from creative selection. The director's preferred take goes in the selects notes; the transfer record still needs to cover every take in the batch. Track technical readiness in an Aspect custom status field and assign someone to update it:[approving a comment and changing an asset's approval status are separate actions](https://aspect.inc/docs/review-and-approve/approvals) .


## Have the editor check the delivery on their own workstation


Noor checks the receiving end using the account, workstation, and editing application that will be used for the project. This exposes missing permissions, incorrect media paths, or absent support files before the editor starts building a sequence around them.


On macOS or Windows, Noor installs the Aspect desktop app, receives project access, and[mounts the project](https://aspect.inc/docs/instant-access/mount-a-project) . Import the agreed media from that mounted location and keep its folder names stable after acceptance. Shared media access and editing-project collaboration remain separate jobs; use the editing application's project-sharing or ownership controls for changes to the edit.


Noor checks the imported clip inventory, attaches the proxies where required, and compares several frames and sound positions against their sources. Confirm that the project reopens with the expected media online. If the originals are still arriving, record which checks remain pending and when they will be completed.


The editor compares received frames and sound while another source item is still in transit. For an unreliable connection,[pin the needed media](https://aspect.inc/docs/instant-access/pin-files) and wait for the complete download before the session. Include sound, proxies, graphics, and project files. Pinning a project file doesn't fetch its references, and previously playing a clip doesn't mean every byte is available offline.


## Close the handoff with a specific acceptance record


Keep the delivery details in one note that you and the person receiving the files can both use. Use this checklist for each batch:


- **Identity:** Record the project, shoot date, batch ID, camera rolls, sound rolls, and sender and receiver names.
- **Completeness:** Compare expected and received camera clips, sound files, total files, and byte counts. List exclusions explicitly.
- **Integrity:** Include the source manifest, verification method, destination results, and any receiving verification still required.
- **Source and proxy matching:** Confirm source filenames, roll IDs, timecode, frame rate, duration, proxy relationships, and sound layout.
- **Viewing checks:** Record the look version, viewing target, sync checks, review coverage, and known picture or sound issues.
- **Access:** Confirm that the recipient can open the review set and the agreed media for editing with the permissions provided.
- **Acceptance:** Record the time, accepted scope, unresolved items, next owner, and deadline. Keep camera-card release as its own authorized decision.


For example, Maya's inventory might list 54 clips from A021 and 32 from B014, plus nine sound files. If Noor finds two proxies with the wrong audio layout, the delivery note should identify those two clips and Luis's correction deadline. Noor can accept the other 84 clips for editing while leaving those exceptions open, if Rowan agrees to that partial handoff.


When the replacements arrive, Noor checks their source matches and sound again, then updates the acceptance record. Keep that record with the batch so the editor can see what arrived, which checks passed, and who is handling anything still outstanding.


## FAQ


Include the agreed review files and media for editing, a source-to-proxy mapping, production sound, camera and sound reports, color references, and a delivery manifest. The manifest should identify each camera roll, expected clip counts, file counts and sizes, checksum records, known exceptions, and the people responsible for sending and accepting the batch. Original-media delivery may follow a different schedule, but its status must remain explicit.


No. Upload completion and source-to-destination checksum verification are separate checks. Keep the reports from the original offload, reconcile the uploaded inventory, and perform receiving verification against the source manifest whenever the production requires a verified receiving copy. A playable preview doesn't establish that every original file and sidecar arrived intact.


Browser previews are useful for watching and reviewing footage, but editing proxies must satisfy the editing application's requirements. Aspect can copy videos as smaller MP4 proxies. Before attaching them, check the source relationship, timecode, frame rate, duration, and audio layout. Create separate proxies when the generated copies don't meet the project's requirements.


The production's written media policy should identify the person who can authorize card release and the evidence they require. The offload operator supplies verification results for each required destination and records any errors. Neither a cloud upload notification nor an editor watching a daily replaces that release decision.


Arrange access before the session and make the required media available locally in advance. With Aspect on macOS or Windows, mount the project, pin the needed files or folders, and wait for pinning to finish. Include proxies, sound, graphics, and the project file; pinning the project file alone doesn't download its referenced media. Open the intended sequence and check playback before relying on offline access.
